title: Raft membership, quorum, and leadership transitions
purpose: Find latent consensus-safety and availability failures in quorum formation, leadership transitions, membership mutation, Raft transport, request forwarding, ReadIndex certification, and Raft snapshot installation without re-auditing pure FSM/cache mechanics or downstream worker lifecycle ownership.
invariants: Valid historical remove/add/remove cycles at one ordinal replay in one Ready or across delayed cleanup without conflicts. Each committed removal retains independent identity admission protection until its durable applied index and matching tuple tombstone are verified; exact duplicates reuse the event, same-index contradictory identities fail, and stale cleanup cannot release another event. Caller cancellation cannot own protection.

A normal Raft entry or ConfChange becomes committed only under the quorum rules of the configuration that governs that transition; no minority, stale leader, learner, or removed member may acknowledge a successful quorum-dependent operation.

Leadership acquisition must establish an applied local horizon at least as new as the leadership barrier before opening leader-only admission, membership orchestration, forwarding ownership, or quorum-certified reads; leadership loss must fence pending leader-owned operations without reinterpreting a committed outcome as rejected.

A successful mutation or membership response is emitted only after the correlated committed entry has completed its required local durable apply. Cancellation or leadership loss after commit must expose an unknown-or-committed outcome with enough stable evidence to avoid resolving a later operation's waiter.

Normal add, learner promotion, update, and removal operations serialize valid ConfChange transitions, preserve voter/learner roles and identity, and converge the Raft ConfState plus replicated membership state on every surviving replica.

A member removed after joining with an instance identity cannot silently rejoin or be promoted under that same identity. Every cluster member carries a mandatory 16-byte instance_id enforced at every admission, persistence, and promotion boundary; identity-less phantom members are no longer a supported state.

Force removal remains an explicitly unsafe, leader-local recovery operation: it must enforce its operator preconditions, persist the reduced ConfState before peer/tombstone cleanup, fail-stop after an irreversible live transition whose persistence fails, and converge surviving followers only through the documented snapshot path.

Election authority comes from the Raft log alone: a voter whose store is behind its WAL snapshot (out of sync, or fetching a checkpoint) keeps ticking, votes, and may campaign and win, because its log holds every committed entry; only a node installing a Raft snapshot pauses its clock. Serving authority is separate: joining, restarting, lagging, removed, or snapshot-receiving nodes must not accept transfer, serve quorum-certified reads, admit writes or membership changes, or start event sinks and mirrors with stale authority before their FSM, membership, and durable applied horizons satisfy the documented gate.

Raft transport authentication, stream replacement, disconnect/reconnect, duplicate delivery, and forwarding must preserve message and request identity across terms; transport retries may redeliver Raft messages but must not manufacture a second logical proposal or a false acknowledgement.

A silently blackholed Raft stream must be detected and replaced so a peer can redial its current endpoint and resume message delivery. Sustained healthy traffic or a valid delayed probe response must not cause a false disconnect. A response on the high-priority stream alone does not establish liveness of the medium- or low-priority streams.

ReadIndex request identity must be unique across caller process incarnations and waiter resolution must match the entire opaque context; an unchanged leader/term retaining a pre-restart read certificate cannot authorize a new invocation after a later completed write.

ReadIndex certification requires the active leader and a quorum of the current voter configuration, and the certified index must be applied before the read proceeds. Only an explicitly stale read may bypass that certificate; projection semantics after the barrier belong to read-consistency-projections.

Snapshot send/install must bind compatible Raft metadata, ConfState, FSM snapshot, spool/catch-up state, and peer identity. The receiver must drain conflicting apply work and remain non-serving until installation and subsequent synchronization establish a coherent applied and durable horizon.

Committed entry ordering and membership outcomes must survive leader crash, transfer, restart, retained-log catch-up, and snapshot catch-up without loss, double durable effect, or configuration regression. Pure deterministic FSM/cache correctness after the consensus boundary belongs to fsm-determinism-cache-coverage.

A combined snapshot/entry Ready must preserve its entry suffix in live Storage and after WAL reopen before any peer or local storage acknowledgement, retaining the original entries/HardState durability order.

Controlled drain preflights every current member for protocol support, fences prior membership changes before marker enqueue, and rejects marker or release proposals if leadership term changed since preflight. It blocks normal membership changes from enqueue through applied release. Its completion certificate requires matching current membership and each captured member locally persisting the same cutoff; leader Match alone is insufficient.
adversarial_questions: When production learner join preflight commits membership before the joining Raft listener starts, does a failed first optional-TLS probe retain both the committed endpoint and a live retry owner? After listener startup, can ordinary traffic recover replication, catch-up and automatic promotion without re-registration or voter restart, while removal and shutdown terminate pending retries?

Does an interrupted cluster command return retryable Unavailable when its Raft run has stopped, including wrapped raft.ErrStopped, while unrelated failures retain their sanitized error classification?

Can one follower Ready contain several removals at a reused ordinal before async FSM submission? Do all identity guards survive canceled foreground waits, delayed cleanup, duplicate observations and restart while fresh identities remain eligible? Does cleanup delete only the original node/index/pointer after durable tombstone verification, and is lookup confined to that ordinal's pending history?

At each transition from follower or candidate to leader, what exact index is drained/applied before leader-only admission, learner promotion, forwarding ownership, and leadership notifications become effective, and can a concurrent step-down reopen a stale path?

What happens when leadership changes after request admission, proposal enqueue, Raft acceptance, quorum commit, ConfChange observation, local durable apply, or immediately before response delivery? Which identity correlates the response or committed-unknown error to the original operation?

Can two concurrent add, promote, remove, force-remove, update, or rejoin requests bypass pending-ConfChange serialization, reuse a node ID with the wrong instance ID, or allow a delayed committed ConfChange to resolve a newer waiter?

For every voter-set transition, which old/new/joint configuration determines quorum at proposal, commit, election, ReadIndex, and transfer time, and can an isolated former leader or removed voter still produce an externally successful result?

Can a removed identified member re-enter through JoinAsLearner, direct AddLearner, bootstrap discovery, auto-promotion, restart, or stale leader admission before the replicated tombstone or pending-removal barrier is visible?

For force removal, what durable state remains after interruption between live ApplyConfChange, snapshot-file replacement, WAL snapshot-record append, peer deletion, and tombstone write, and does every persistence-error branch stop serving before any reduced unpersisted quorum can commit?

Can an outstanding leader-side ReadIndex at C survive a follower restart with the same member identity, leader and term, then resolve a new read after a write D > C completes? Trace full context matching, delayed heartbeat acknowledgements and responses, rejection of legacy and duplicate contexts, and the subsequent local applied-index barrier.

Can a lagging or syncing node accept MsgTimeoutNow, complete ReadIndex, admit writes or membership changes, start event sinks or mirrors, or serve a forwarded mutation before spool replay and snapshot synchronization reach the required index? When such a node wins an election on its log, which store-dependent path opens before its checkpoint sync and spool replay complete, and does its checkpoint donor rotation reach a voter whose store is current?

Can retained-log compaction, snapshot selection, transfer interruption, sender restart, or receiver restart combine an incompatible ConfState with FSM/store contents, regress applied indexes, or discard entries committed after the snapshot?

Can simultaneous transport connections, stale streams, protocol/authentication rejection, reconnect queues, duplicate messages, or unreachable notifications cross terms or peer incarnations and affect the wrong active connection or Raft node?

After an old peer address silently blackholes traffic and discovery points to a replacement endpoint, does the outbound connection detect the missing probe response or blocked send, close the old attempt, redial, and deliver a Raft message? Can continuously nonempty priority queues starve probe scheduling, or can a valid delayed response, stale response, or response from another stream incorrectly reset the deadline or close a healthy connection?

When a committed ConfChangeUpdateNode refreshes an existing peer address, do Pebble, the membership cache, and the operational Raft and service connection pools converge before the next Raft tick without recreating the peer identity or send loop? Does a transient optional-TLS probe failure during the address refresh preserve the committed target for the loop's next retry, or does it strand the peer with no active retry owner?

Can a follower-to-leader forwarded request loop, fall back locally without a valid leader/barrier, lose cancellation or committed-outcome metadata, or be executed twice because transport identity is confused with logical proposal identity?

Which immediate leadership observers update routing and membership authority synchronously, and can their failure expose stale authority? Deep goroutine ownership, cancellation, shutdown joins, and event/mirror/backup worker generations belong to concurrency-lifecycle-shutdown.
Can snapshot installation discard entries carried by the same Ready, and what in-memory snapshot/cache state and durable WAL prefix remain if suffix restoration fails before storage acknowledgement?

Can a mixed-version member pass preflight, or can a membership change slip between preflight and marker application? If leadership is lost and regained after preflight while another leader changes membership, does the old-term marker or release get rejected before Raft append? Can a timed-out marker, lost member, leader transfer or force removal make the operator accept an obsolete captured set or a follower that has not persisted the cutoff?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: hold a fresh learner's listener closed through production join preflight with optional TLS, record the current term, committed addition index, durable membership and valid instance identity, then open the listener and require autonomous replication and promotion without another registration; independently test initial probe fail-then-success, actual Raft stream delivery, endpoint replacement, and pending-owner removal/shutdown (internal/bootstrap/join_transport_recovery_test.go and internal/infra/node/transport_initial_probe_test.go)

replay remove(A), add(B), remove(B) through a real follower RawNode Ready and WAL restart; compare with durable apply between changes, retain both tombstones, delay cleanup across newer events, cancel foreground waits, and test duplicate observation, same-index contradictory identity, stale pointer deletion and per-ordinal cost shape

retain a leader-side read at C across follower RawNode reconstruction from retained MemoryStorage, commit distinguishable write D > C through the other voters, deliver the delayed old response in the unchanged term, and prove production waiter resolution rejects it while a fresh certificate waits for D to be locally applied (internal/infra/node/read_index_restart_test.go); also verify old eight-byte and new opaque contexts are echoed unchanged

Run the Antithesis cross-node identity oracle against complete current membership at an exact durable horizon, with final per-node/global/membership fences before verdict publication. Inject missing or different account/audit state, an unavailable member, late writes, changed membership and incomplete paginated streams; failed qualification must not become a successful or corrupt-data observation. Operational witnesses must retain and compare exact acknowledged transaction content, and post-transfer write coverage requires a new acknowledged business write rather than a leader ID alone.
